That distinction and safeguard feel right. Inside Edit I chose "Delete bookmark," got a clear warning that it couldn't be undone, and after confirming "Delete permanently" the JavaScript Guide was gone from my collection — and when I opened Archive it stayed empty, with a note that deleted bookmarks aren't moved there. So delete really does remove it for good and doesn't behave like archive's reversible tuck-away. That's exactly the difference I wanted: archive to hide things I might revisit, delete for things I want truly gone.

Having permanent delete live inside Edit behind an explicit "this can't be undone" step reassures me I won't nuke something by accident.

I'm happy with archiving and delete. What's next?
